business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Home Hydroponics and Gardening Equipment

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus) — active regional free trade agreement
No bilateral investment treaty currently in force with the People's Republic of China; no double tax agreement currently in force for Samoa International Companies.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa) as amended; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (Samoa); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2000; Proceeds of Crime Act 2007; International Companies (Amendment) Act 2010 concerning beneficial owner registration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the beneficial owner's passport bio-data page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the beneficial owner's country of residence / National Immigration Administration or equivalent passport-issuance authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if both countries are parties; otherwise dual consular legalization (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of origin jurisdiction and Samoan Embassy or Honorary Consul)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within previous 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the address jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization to certify the true copy, followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial owner declaration and personal due diligence questionnaire (including source of funds and source of wealth disclosure)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SIFSA-licensed registered agent / AML compliance officer; declaration executed before a notary public or immediate agent officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized officer certificate; Apostille required if the declaration is executed by a foreign public notary abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) domestic list, OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, UK Financial Sanctions List, and the Samoa Consolidated Sanctions List. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified using FATF methodology; enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs regardless of the 25% ownership threshold. All screening must be conducted immediately upon receipt and updated at least every 30 days during onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) e-Registry — Company Registration and Name Reservation Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed company names must be registered in English or a Latin-character romanization. Names in Chinese characters or non-Latin scripts are not registrable as the sole legal name; an English phonetic transliteration and the Chinese character name may be included in the Memorial or Articles as a parallel reference only. Such parallel reference must be submitted to SIFSA for administrative notation but does not create a distinct statutory name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant receives a written notice citing the specific ground of rejection under the International Companies Act 1987 and the General Companies Regulations. The applicant, through its licensed registered agent, may file a written appeal with the Registrar within 14 days after notice, together with supporting submissions and, if necessary, a formal request for ministerial approval for sensitive tokens. If the Registrar upholds rejection, judicial review may be pursued before the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days from the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office; every Samoa International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa through a SIFSA-licensed agent, where formal notices, process, and corporate records may be served. For this e-commerce and garden hydroponics equipment online retail activity, a virtual office may be used only for ancillary back-office or customer-service functions and does not satisfy registered-office or commercial-substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximately 2% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in any given compliance year for a low-risk e-commerce entity with no regulated activities. Probability increases to roughly 15% if the company triggers a suspicious activity report, sanctions hit, or a PEP-related red flag.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended — statutory incorporation, name reservation, registered office and registered agent requirements, appointment of directors and officers, and statutory exemption from Samoan income tax and stamp duty; supplemented by the Companies (Fees) Regulations and the licensed registered-agent regime administered under the same Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa — filings made exclusively through a licensed International Company registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation together with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association; formal issuance of a Certificate of Incorporation by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Samoa International Company; share capital may be expressed in any currency, shares may be issued at no par value and remain wholly or partially unpaid. Where voluntary paid-in capital is introduced for bank onboarding, funds may be held in a client escrow account maintained by the licensed registered agent or the receiving bank until the corporate bank account is opened.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] — BE IT RESOLVED as follows: (1) The subscriber shares in the Company are hereby allotted and issued to the initial shareholder, and the register of members is updated accordingly. (2) The registered office of the Company is hereby fixed at the registered agent's licensed address in Apia, Samoa, and the registered agent is authorized to accept service of process on the Company's behalf. (3) [Director Name] is appointed as Director and [Secretary Name] as Secretary, each to hold office until removed by ordinary resolution. (4) The officers are authorized to open bank accounts and engage professional advisers for the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and compliance pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia — via licensed registered agent (no direct public lodgment for International Companies).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed registered agent to submit a Form IC-1 name-clearance request with two preferred names in English. The agent verifies that the proposed name is not identical or deceptively similar to an existing Samoa company, does not contain restricted words (Bank, Trust, Insurance, etc.) without approval, and is acceptable to the Registrar under the name provisions of the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 name clearance request
Certified copy of passport of ultimate beneficial owner(s)
Proof of agent's client due-diligence file
Proposed English company name (primary and secondary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or requisitioned, the agent resubmits the secondary name or a modified name within 5 business days; a conflict with a prior registrant is cured by the prior registrant's written consent or by adding a distinguishing prefix/suffix to the proposed name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, notarization and apostille of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction; Apostille/Authentication authority of that jurisdiction; ultimate filing to the MCIL Registrar via the licensed registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The shareholder executes the Memorandum and Articles of Association before a notary public. Witness signatures must be notarially certified; if execution occurs in a State party to the Apostille Convention (Samoa is a party), affix an apostille. The licensed registered agent reviews the executed pack for consistency with Samoan form requirements and the cleared name, then prepares signed Consent to Act forms of the first director and first secretary.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association executed by subscriber
Notarial certificate (and apostille where applicable)
Consent to Act of the first director
Consent to Act of the first secretary
Consent of the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective signature pages or witness attestations are cured within 14 days by re-executing only the defective pages; if the document version differs from the name-clearance proof, the corrected version is re-lodged with a cover letter confirming no substantive change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment of incorporation application and payment of statutory fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL International Companies Registry, Apia, Samoa (filing counter or registry e-lodgment facility, submitted by the licensed registered agent).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent lodges the application for incorporation with the executed constitutional documents, consent forms, and the prescribed filing fee (USD 100 government incorporation fee plus annual license component), payable in WST equivalent by bank transfer or agent's trust account. The application must state the registered office in Samoa and identify the licensed registered agent.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 application for incorporation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consents of first director and first secretary
Registered agent consent and registered office address
Fee payment receipt (WST/USD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition under the Act, the agent has 14 days to file corrections or clarifications; a deemed withdrawal may be cured by filing a fresh application with a waiver or refund of one fee cycle, and any refusal is subject to internal review by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance and custody of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia, Samoa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfaction of all filing requirements the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation in the English language, recording the company number, name, date of incorporation, and registered office. The licensed agent obtains the certificate, affixes the company seal if one is adopted, and places it in custody together with the statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Register of members
Register of directors and officers
Registered office and registered agent particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Administrative typographical errors in the certificate (company number, name, date) are corrected by a written request to the Registrar accompanied by the original certificate; substantive corrections follow the statutory alteration procedure and re-certification within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board written resolution and statutory book setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors and licensed registered agent of the Company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole or first director passes the pro-forma first board written resolution recorded above, allotting subscriber shares to the initial shareholder, fixing the registered office at the agent's licensed address, appointing the director and secretary, and authorizing bank account opening. The resolution is filed in the minute book, the register of members is completed, and share certificates are issued.
required_dossiers: First board written resolution
Notice of meeting or waiver of notice (if a meeting is held)
Register of members and share certificates
Register of directors and officers
Registered agent acknowledgement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An incomplete minute is ratified at the next board meeting or by a supplementary written resolution signed by all directors; a defective share allotment is confirmed by a validating resolution recorded in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax-exempt status confirmation and depositary or bank onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Ministry for Revenue (tax status confirmation); commercial banks and payment-rail acquirers (Stripe, PayPal) for onboarding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Rely on the statutory income-tax exemption of International Companies and, where requested by a bank or payment processor, obtain a Certificate of Tax Exemption from the Samoa Ministry for Revenue confirming the Company's exempt status. Present the Certificate of Incorporation, first board resolution, register of members and UBO due-diligence pack to the acquiring bank or payment-rail processor for account or merchant activation. E-commerce sales are directed at offshore customers; no Samoan business licence is triggered.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Certificate of Tax Exemption (where issued)
First board resolution authorizing bank accounts
UBO/KYC due-diligence pack
Business plan or sales-channel description for merchant onboarding (Stripe/PayPal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment processor requests economic-substance or source-of-funds clarification, provide an accountant's letter confirming the Company's offshore e-commerce operations, the absence of Samoan-resident customers, and the statutory prohibition on carrying on business in Samoa.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no physical manufacturing, warehousing or retail establishment is located in Samoa; the Company is an International Company that is statutorily restricted from carrying on business with Samoan residents, and all sales occur through online channels to offshore customers. The Business Licences Act 2001 licensing trigger is therefore not engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for the offshore e-commerce activity. For completeness, if the Company later decided to import or warehouse goods in Samoa, it would require a Business Licence under the Business Licences Act 2001 and, for any horticultural equipment containing agrochemical or biosecurity-sensitive accessories, an import permit under the relevant biosecurity regime administered by the Ministry of Agriculture.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) and Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Samoa.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical installation, land alteration or stationary emission source is proposed in Samoa; remote online retail and third-party drop-shipping do not constitute a 'project' requiring an EIA under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial discharge is generated in Samoa; no wastewater, VOC or hazardous-emission permit is applicable to the registered activity. Packaging and shipping materials handled at overseas fulfilment centres are subject to the local waste regime of that jurisdiction; if any goods transit Samoa, the Waste Management Act 2005 standards apply, including prohibitions on open burning and uncontrolled disposal, together with the duty of care on waste transferors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for the offshore operation, which has no employees or physical premises in Samoa. If the licensed registered agent's suite in Apia is occupied by an administrative service provider, the occupier must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002 (fire extinguisher provision, emergency egress, sanitation) and Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority requirements for office occupancies; no structural-load inspection or fire certificate is triggered for a desk-based serviced office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), the national tax administration agency; portal: SRA eServices (https://www.sra.gov.ws). Company registration is filed separately with the International Companies Office (ICO), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 is, without more, outside the Samoan income tax net and is not required to obtain a Samoan TIN for offshore business. If the IC seeks GST/VAT registration in Samoa (e.g., to acquire zero-rating/refund capacity or to make Samoan taxable supplies), it must apply to SRA on the prescribed GST registration form, providing: (i) International Company certificate of incorporation and memorandum/articles; (ii) identification of directors and shareholders; (iii) Samoan registered office and appointed agent details; (iv) description of supplies and expected annual turnover; and (v) bank account or receipt evidence. SRA verifies the application and issues a TIN/GST registration number. Non-resident foreign corporations with no Samoan place of business generally do not need a TIN unless an obligation such as withholding tax, GST registration, or physical economic activity arises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. An International Company may elect to be taxed as an ordinary Samoa resident company by re-registering under the Companies Act 2001 (thereby surrendering IC tax-exempt status), and may elect to voluntarily register for GST if it makes or intends to make taxable supplies. SRA may also issue binding rulings concerning GST treatment of offshore or export arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Goods and Services Tax, GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 of annual taxable supplies (compulsory); voluntary registration is available below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, API filing, or digital stamping regime is in force for Samoa. GST-registered persons must issue prescribed tax invoices and credit notes, retain records (generally seven years), and file periodic GST returns through the SRA eServices portal or paper returns. SRA is developing digital services but no continuous transaction control mandate currently exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to a GST-registered supplier's export of movable goods where the goods are physically exported from Samoa and shipped to a non-resident within the time specified in the GST Act, and to international services directly related to exported goods or physically performed outside Samoa for a non-resident. The supplier must retain documentary evidence proving movement, the non-resident customer, and the receivable. An offshore e-commerce IC whose goods are never imported into or exported from Samoa will not meet Samoa export zero-rating conditions; it generally remains outside the Samoan GST net rather than claiming zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs export declaration / exit manifest
Ocean bill of lading or air waybill showing Samoa port or airport of departure
Commercial invoice and sale contract stating export terms (e.g., FOB/EXW)
Packing list / container stuffing records where applicable
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency bank credit evidence from the Samoan banking system
Certificate or other evidence of the non-resident status of the buyer or offshore service recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SRA scrutinizes zero-rating claims by cross-checking customs, banking and returns data. Goods or services that were not actually exported or that lack the prescribed evidence within the statutory period are treated as taxable at 15%; the resulting GST, default assessment and late-payment penalties are immediately clawed back. Filing false export declarations or using artificial arrangements to claim refunds may attract criminal sanctions, personal liability of directors, and substantial civil penalties, in addition to interest and loss of refund offsets.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) — statutory monetary and exchange control authority established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; foreign exchange administration is additionally governed by the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1984, together with periodic CBS Exchange Control Notices issued to all licensed authorized dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates a managed exchange-control regime centered on the Samoan Tala (WST), which is not freely convertible offshore. Current-account transactions (trade in goods and services, interest, royalties, and ordinary profit remittances) have been substantially liberalized: authorized dealer banks may process such payments without case-by-case CBS approval provided full underlying documentation is lodged. Capital-account transactions — including equity injections, shareholder loans, and repatriation of invested capital — remain subject to prior CBS approval, although payments of profits, dividends, and liquidation proceeds by tax-exempt International Companies (ICs) registered under the International Companies Act 2019 (including the WS_IC entity) are normally approved without substantive tax review given the IC operates in a tax-exempt zone. In practice, the WS_IC's e-commerce treasury is structured to collect USD revenue offshore through payment aggregators (Stripe and PayPal) and to retain those proceeds in foreign-currency accounts; conversion into WST is required only where the entity maintains onshore WST operational balances. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal for ICs but banks must nevertheless verify source of funds, payment-processor settlement statements, and underlying sales contracts before executing cross-border credit transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1984 and current CBS policy, exporters of goods or services must collect payment no later than three (3) months after the date of export/supply, remit the full proceeds into Samoa through a licensed authorized dealer, and surrender 100% of the foreign currency into Tala (WST) within thirty (30) days of receipt unless a specific CBS exemption has been granted. The Central Bank may, upon written application, permit a foreign-currency retention account or partial deferral of conversion where the exporter demonstrates recurring foreign-currency liabilities (e.g., USD-denominated supplier settlements for hydroponics equipment procurement), but such approval must be secured in advance and is reviewed annually. E-commerce sellers settling through Stripe/PayPal are treated as exporters of services/goods for exchange-control reporting purposes; the WS_IC must therefore furnish periodic proof of payment-processor settlement and, absent an exemption, route net proceeds to its Samoa bank account within the mandated timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Foreign-Currency and WST Account
Operational Account / USD and WST Current Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Samoa does not maintain a stand-alone licensing regime for electronic money institutions (EMIs) or digital-only cross-border banks; the Financial Institutions Act 2019 does not recognize offshore EMI charters as eligible for onshore banking licenses. As such, foreign fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, or licensed EU/UK EMI entities) cannot obtain a Samoa banking license or direct settlement access at CBS. Their functionality is limited to acting as non-bank payment intermediaries supported by correspondent banks; accordingly, for WS_IC treasury purposes, the use of such platforms is legally permissible only as payment-collection or payment-disbursement conduits, not as the primary regulated bank account holder. The registered commercial banks in Samoa remain the sole onshore deposit-taking and FX-conversion counterparties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, but in practice all four onshore banks require at least one authorized signatory (typically the director or the licensed registered agent acting as an authorized signatory) to complete an in-person identity verification interview at the bank's head office in Apia before account opening. Remote account opening is available but strictly conditional: the applicant must provide notarized/certified copies of passports, a banker's confirmation letter from the applicant's home-country bank, and undergo a video-verification call with the bank's compliance officer; the registered agent under the International Companies Act 2019 must countersign the KYC pack. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies automatically to non-face-to-face openings, extending onboarding timelines. Directors of the WS_IC who are not physically present during the interview should expect a hold on transaction authority until the videographic verification and certified document chain are fully completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore IC structure exhibiting nominee directorship or undisclosed ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incumbency and Register of Directors/Shareholders issued by the licensed registered agent; statutory declaration of the registered agent identifying the natural-person UBO; certified copies of passport of each director and shareholder; certificate of good standing from the Samoa International Companies Registry; corporate constitutional documents (Memorandum and Articles of Association) duly stamped.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding flagged as high-risk due to remote jurisdiction and absence of economic substance evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan for online retail of home hydroponics and gardening equipment; e-commerce marketplace verification (Stripe and PayPal seller identification, storefront URLs, settlement history); supply-chain contracts with equipment manufacturers and logistics providers; warehouse or fulfillment-center agreements; six months of bank statements from the home-country operating account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for initial capital injection and subsequent operational deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement signed by the UBO; domestic bank statements covering the 12 months preceding onboarding; tax residency certificate of the UBO; evidence of legitimate commercial earnings (platform settlement reports, invoices, and payment receipts); declaration confirming that the WS International Company relies on the statutory tax-exempt regime and does not rely on traded securities or virtual-asset revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media screening failure against named directors, shareholders, or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current passport scans and independent sanctions-screen reports (World-Check or equivalent) commissioned through the registered agent; sworn affidavits from the directors explaining any name-match hits; third-party legal opinion confirming the individuals are not listed persons; AML training certificates and corporate policies for the WS_IC confirming adherence to Oro-generated transaction monitoring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections — whether shareholder loans or equity subscription funds — must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COVER where an intermediary bank is used) from the parent/shareholder's home-country bank to the WS_IC's Samoa operational account. The wire instruction must state the purpose of payment as 'Share Capital Contribution — WS International Company' or 'Shareholder Loan Disbursement', using the Balance of Payments classification codes applicable under CBS reporting: Direct Investment — Equity Capital for share subscriptions, and Other Investment — Loans for shareholder advances. The receiving authorized dealer is required to verify the underlying resolution of the board of directors, the share allotment/loan agreement, and the UBO identification evidence before crediting the account. CBS prior approval is required when the initial injection exceeds the standard authorized-dealer threshold; in such case, a CBS Exchange Control application must accompany the bank, including audited financial projections evidencing the e-commerce working-capital requirement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for hydroponics-equipment procurement from overseas suppliers are settled primarily by SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for invoice payments under USD purchase orders. For larger or recurring shipments where the supplier demands documentary security, a commercial letter of credit (MT700) may be opened through Bank of Samoa or Samoa Commercial Bank, with documents drawn including the commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/airway bill, and certificate of origin. Settlement cycles must align with the CBS reporting calendar: the bank requires underlying contracts, proforma invoices, and supplier KYC on file so that each disbursement is tagged with the appropriate purpose code (General Merchandise — Imports) and submitted for CBS balance-of-payments aggregation. Where the WS_IC retains USD in a foreign-currency retention account, supplier wires may be effected directly in USD without WST conversion, thereby reducing FX friction; payroll, rent, and domestic Samoan obligations would be settled from a WST sub-account funded by the 30-day conversion rule applicable to export receipts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/WST spot transactions executed through authorized dealer banks with full CBS reporting.

Forward foreign-exchange contracts (deliverable USD/WST forwards) booked with a licensed Samoa commercial bank, permitted for trade-related exposures and requiring an underlying commercial invoice or purchase order.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offshore against the WST, permissible only where the counterparty is a reputable international bank and the WS_IC either holds an offshore treasury account or maintains adequate credit support; such NDF transactions are generally outside CBS onshore regulatory perimeter but must be disclosed to the onshore bank for consolidated reporting.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) with authorized dealers for the purpose of refinancing shareholder loans or hedging committed e-commerce treasury flows, subject to CBS case-by-case approval when the swap term exceeds 12 months.

Natural hedging via foreign-currency retention accounts denominated in USD, allowing matched inflows from Stripe/PayPal settlement and outflows to overseas suppliers, thereby minimizing the need for explicit derivative instruments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government License Fee (Annual Renewal Fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on or before the anniversary of incorporation, with a 30-day grace period before late fees accrue.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 10% late-payment surcharge applies after the grace period; continued non-payment for approximately 3 months triggers a Registrar strike-off notice, leading to dissolution and forfeiture of assets to the State.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Compliance Confirmation (Good Standing Certification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent and registered office; certification made available to Registrar on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary, and immediately upon any change of registered agent or registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent and registered office in Samoa is an offence under the International Companies Act 2008 and is a statutory ground for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Register Confirmation (UBO Update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and Registrar of International Companies, filed by the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary; any share-transfer driven UBO change must be recorded within 14 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and the registered agent commit an offence for non-compliance; fines up to SAT 10,000 (approximately USD 3,600) plus AML/CFT enforcement penalties apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of Change of Directors, Members or Registered Office (if any)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days of the relevant change; a nil-change position is covered by the annual renewal declaration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the company and its registered agent to monetary penalties; persistent default may result in administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: No Annual Return or Audited Financial Statements Filing (Statutory Exemption)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not applicable; exemption codified under the International Companies Act 2008 - no filing is required with the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: None applicable; good standing is preserved solely by timely payment of the annual government license fee.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory threshold: a Samoa International Company is exempt from independent audit unless (i) its Memorandum and Articles require an audit, (ii) shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights demand an audit, or (iii) it operates licensed banking, insurance, or trust business subject to Samoa's regulated sector supervision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No compulsory accounting framework for tax-exempt international companies; voluntary financial statements should be prepared in accordance with IFRS as adopted in Samoa. No tax filings arise from the offshore tax-exempt status.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at the registered office and confirm it annually to the Registrar/FIU through the registered agent within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary. Every transfer of shares that changes beneficial ownership must be entered in the register and notified within 14 days; the annual confirmation restates all material ownership data.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Zero by default (exempt); voluntary audit market range approximately USD 3,000 - USD 5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for an International Company on offshore-sourced income; 27% standard corporate income tax rate applies if the IC generates Samoan-source income or is deemed resident due to domestic business activity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption for International Companies: no Samoan income tax on foreign-source profits, no capital gains tax, no withholding tax on shareholder distributions, and no stamp duty on offshore transactions. Qualifying domestic investment projects may obtain Cabinet-approved tax holidays up to 5 years under Samoa's investment incentive laws, but an online retail IC does not ordinarily qualify.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Annual Return (Form IC-AR) filed through the Samoa Companies Office eRegistry; no Samoan corporate income tax return is required for a tax-exempt International Company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation; the first filing is due within 60 days after the first anniversary date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the International Company exactly as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact English name; do not insert a trade name alone. The registered agent must verify name consistency with the Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique IC registration number assigned by the Samoa Companies Office at incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the number with the IC prefix, e.g., IC-12345. No leading zeros or punctuation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical Samoa registered office address and licensed registered agent contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Overseas directors cannot nominate a foreign address here. The licensed Samoa agent must sign and confirm the registered office details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Register of Directors and Shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current list of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners, including any changes since the last annual return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide passport, nationality, and beneficial ownership details. Under Samoa's AML legislation, the ultimate natural person controllers must be disclosed, even if held through nominee arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that no local (Samoan-source) business was conducted during the financial year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an online garden hydroponics equipment vendor, confirm that all remote sales are to non-Samoan customers. Any sale to a person in Samoa may require a local business license and destroy the tax-exempt character.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the IC did not solicit gross revenue from the Samoan public, maintain a physical store, warehouse, or office staff in Samoa, or contract with Samoan residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tick 'No local solicitation'. Using local couriers solely for occasional deliveries is not itself a Samoan business, but systematic local delivery, customer support, or advertising to Samoan residents is prohibited without licensing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement confirming that the IC holds no liability for Samoan income tax and is not in arrears of annual registry fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No profit and loss account is required. Nonetheless, retain proper accounting records offshore for at least 7 years to substantiate the offshore-source character of revenue if challenged by Samoa Revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a daily surcharge of WST 20 per day, capped at WST 2,000, plus the underlying annual fee. Continued default beyond 6 months permits the Registrar to strike off the IC without a court order; restoration requires payment of all arrears and a reinstatement fee of WST 300. Where a director knowingly causes default, a fine of up to WST 5,000 and imprisonment of up to 3 months may be imposed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends and other distributions paid by a Samoan International Company to non-resident shareholders. By contrast, a domestic resident company is subject to a standard 15% non-resident dividend withholding tax, unless reduced under an applicable Double Tax Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Ministry of Revenue, complete Form IR-WHT (WHT Treaty Reduction Application), and provide a Letter of Explanation together with supporting beneficial ownership evidence to the payor or withholding agent before the payment date. The Ministry of Revenue ordinarily processes the ruling within 30 business days. Excess withheld amounts may be recovered by filing an annual refund claim. For a non-resident owned International Company, treaty relief is normally unnecessary because the IC distribution is not subject to Samoan WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For a Samoan International Company, cross-border royalties and debt interest paid to non-residents in respect of the IC's offshore business are exempt from Samoan withholding tax. For a domestic resident payer, statutory WHT rates are 15% on interest and 15% on royalties; certain DTA counterparts reduce interest and royalties to 10%, and technical service fees may be exempt under some UN Model-based conventions. Treaty relief requires a TRC and pre-approval by the Ministry of Revenue.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: International Companies in the wholly tax-exempt regime have no mandatory transfer pricing documentation obligation because they are outside the income tax net. If an IC loses exemption or elects to pay Samoan tax on domestic-source business, Samoa's Income Tax Act 2015 requires a Transfer Pricing Local File where related-party transactions exceed WST 2,000,000 (approximately USD 740,000), or related-party debt exceeds WST 1,000,000. A Master File threshold of WST 50,000,000 in group revenue applies for multinational groups entering the Samoan documentation framework.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not impose BVI/Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) on International Companies. However, the IC must maintain a licensed registered agent and a registered office in Samoa. If the IC seeks to use an agreement tied to Samoa tax residence or claims a DTA benefit, Samoa Revenue may apply a general anti-avoidance principal-purpose test and require factual substance: local premises, employees, and real decision-making. Without such substance, the IC may be deemed a shell and denied treaty benefits, and the corporate status may be reconstructed as a local resident company on Samoan-source income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Annual Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly declaring that no Samoan-source business occurred while maintaining local customers, local inventory, a Samoan pay account, or commercial premises; concealing internet sales delivered into Samoa; or manufacturing fictitious offshore sales records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: An additional tax assessment at 27% CIT on all undeclared Samoan-source income, plus interest at 10% per annum and an evasion penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded. Criminal prosecution may result in a court fine of up to WST 250,000 for the company and mandatory disclosure of the IC's full tax affairs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knew or ought to have known of the false declaration are jointly and severally liable for all corporation tax, interest, and evasion penalties. On conviction, a director may face imprisonment for up to 7 years, a personal fine of up to WST 50,000, and a Ministry of Revenue departure ban prohibiting exit from Samoa until the liability is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Samoan International Company with no office, staff, or decision-making in Samoa while using Samoan tax certificates to extract DTA benefits in source jurisdictions; operating in substance from China, Hong Kong, or another jurisdiction while purporting to be a Samoan resident.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits in the source country; Samoa Ministry of Revenue may cancel tax residency certificates, assess penalties of up to WST 50,000 per year of abuse, and retroactively classify the IC as an ordinary domestic resident company on its worldwide income. Foreign tax authorities may also impose secondary transfer pricing adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierceable where the IC is a pure instrumentality. Directors and controlling shareholders may be personally liable for the difference in withholding taxes in the source jurisdiction, plus all Samoan penalties. Where abuse is aggravated, directors face criminal anti-conduit charges with civil asset restitution and a travel ban pending adjudication.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to verify the beneficial ownership of shareholders, using PayPal/Stripe payment routing without customer identification, failing to appoint a Samoa AML compliance officer, or refusing to report suspicious transactions to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act and AML/CFT Rules, the IC and its registered agent face fines up to WST 100,000, suspension of the registered agent's license, freezing of the IC's Samoa and correspondent bank accounts, and forced deregistration. Non-compliance may also result in the IC being blacklisted by correspondent banks and excluded from payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the compliance officer are individually criminally liable if they knowingly permit AML failures. Penalties include fines up to WST 50,000, imprisonment for up to 5 years, civil forfeiture of all proceeds linked to the unregistered e-commerce activity, and a personal travel prohibition in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorised Local Business and Stamp Duty Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An International Company engaging in retail sales to consumers in Samoa, maintaining a Samoan warehouse or fulfilment centre, employing Samoan staff, or using a Samoan bank account without obtaining a local business license and without accounting for VAT, import duties, and income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The International Companies Act exemption is invalidated; the IC is retrospectively assessed as a resident company at 27% tax on all Samoan-source revenue, with an additional unauthorized business penalty of WST 30,000. Samoa Customs and Revenue may also impose duty and VAT (VAGST) on the hydroponics equipment sold or warehoused, plus stop-sale orders against the online portal for Samoa IP addresses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate taxes, duties, penalties, and interest. If the unpaid amounts are fraudulently concealed, directors face criminal sanctions of imprisonment up to 5 years, personal civil restitution, and an asset freeze across Samoa. The court can order a travel ban until all tax liabilities are settled.
